utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. The Chamber has considered Mr. Robinson's request to grant more time for the cross-examination of witness KDZ-474, and has decided to deny it. As indicated to the parties on 21 June 2010 and then noted on several subsequent occasions, the Chamber considers a number of factors when deciding what the appropriate time for cross-examination should be. These include, among other things, the quantity and type of written evidence being tendered, including the number of associated exhibits tendered through Rule 92 ter witnesses, as well as the length of the testimony in the previous case. Accordingly, having considered these factors with respect to Witness KDZ-474, the Chamber decided that 3.5 -- three and a half -- hours more than adequate to cover the issues raised in the witness's anticipated testimony. It remains of the view that this is appropriate for a thorough and efficient cross-examination. While the Chamber does take into account the length of a witness's testimony in a previous case, it does not necessarily follow that the time for cross-examination should be arrived at by adding the time spent on examination-in-chief in the previous case to the time spent on examination-in-chief in this case. As stated before, cross-examination is not an exercise in rehashing the same evidence elicited in various other cases but is an exercise in challenging certain parts of the witness's evidence which are directly relevant to this particular case. Furthermore, as the Chamber indicated many times before, when preparing for cross-examination of Rule 92 ter witnesses, the accused should bear in mind that their cross-examination in the previous case is often also part of the evidence in this case, and thus he should focus his efforts on parts that clearly need further cross-examination or were never properly cross-examined. Finally, the Chamber notes that Mr. Robinson illustrated his submission by using Mr. Panic, whose testimony was completed yesterday, as an example of a witness for whom more time should have been given. However, when asked to point to a specific topic that the accused did not manage to cover with Mr. Panic, Mr. Robinson indicated that the accused was, in fact, able to cover everything. In essence, Mr. Robinson's submission is that the accused should be given substantially more time than he needs in order not to feel rushed or forced into asking compound questions. The Chamber considers, however, that this position is untenable. We repeat our recommendation that Mr. Robinson should advise Mr. Karadzic how to focus his cross-examination on the most relevant issues first and how to avoid lengthy discussion of peripheral issues, as well as to demonstrate to him that asking compound questions in fact wastes more time than it saves. Let us proceed with the evidence. We go back to closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President, in lieu of the witness schedule and the timing of this issue, I wanted to quickly make an oral application for leave to reply to the accused's response to the motion related to videolink, and we would be asking to reply to three different issues: Number 1, the accused's erroneous limitation of the standard for videolink and reliance on that misstated and limited standard found at paragraphs 2 to 3; the accused's reliance on a standard that doesn't exist in the jurisprudence at paragraph 4; and his reliance upon a position already expressly rejected by the Trial Chamber in paragraph 5. I'm not sure that a reply will be deemed necessary by the Chamber. In light of the timing, it may well be that the Chamber is already focusing on that motion and deems it unnecessary. If you do grant this motion, we could certainly be apprised -- you can do it on the spot or we could be apprised tomorrow morning and we would be prepared to respond orally given what I understand to be the timing involved. And when I say respond orally it would be if you did grant us leave I would like the opportunity to at least have a session in between granting and giving the oral reply.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will come back to you tomorrow morning, first thing. But my understanding is that the Registry needs at least 10 days to sets up a videolink.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I understand that the Registry has been in the process for doing so for some time in anticipation of the motion and the possibility that it would be granted so I think preliminary steps and preparations are already underway and that the time -- the normal timing would not be an obstacle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. The hearing is now adjourned --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not certain we tendered page 155 in Serbian and 141 into evidence. We discussed it with the witness and, in particular, those six demands and the final remarks by Talic. This is Rasula's diary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That -- if not, that will be added to the exhibit. I thank again the staff for their indulgence. It has been added. 9.00, tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 22nd day of September, 2011, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.07 p.m.,
